walkthroughs.body_html:
In 2007, for the first time in history, more people lived in cities than in the countryside.

Today around 57% of the world's population is urban. By 2050 it will pass 68%.

Push factors (rural):
- low farm wages, drought, poor schools, no hospitals, conflict.

Pull factors (urban):
- jobs in factories/services, better schools and hospitals, electricity, entertainment, family already there.

A megacity has 10 million+ residents. In 1950 there were only 2 (New York, Tokyo). Today there are over 30.

Most growth is in NEEs and LICs: Lagos, Delhi, Dhaka, Mumbai, Manila, São Paulo. Tokyo is still the world's largest at ~37 million.

mcqs.q: Which is a PULL factor for rural-urban migration?
options: Crop failure
Better job prospects in the city
Conflict in the countryside
Lack of hospitals in villages

mcqs.q: Why do people move from rural to urban areas in LICs?
options: Because cities in poor countries are always better than the countryside.
A combination of push factors (rural poverty, lack of services, agricultural change) and pull factors (perceived jobs, education, healthcare) — though reality often disappoints.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.

mcqs.q: Why do informal settlements develop in rapidly growing LIC cities?
options: People live in slums because they prefer them or are too lazy to find better housing.
Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Rural-urban migration outpaces formal housing supply; migrants build their own homes on marginal land without secure land tenure — driven by housing shortage, not by personal choice.
